notes:
Summary: Velvetecho is a mid-market SaaS product analytics company evaluating Redwood for embedding + semantic search. Priority is fast time-to-value on Hosted API for POC, then move to Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation.

Key requirements:
- Workload: nightly batch embedding jobs (ETL -> embed -> index) plus low-latency query layer for product docs and support KB. Expected steady-state: 1000 QPS read for search layer during peak, average 100 QPS; write/ingest is batch-oriented (target 150-300k embeddings/hour during windows).
- Vector DB integration: currently using Postgres + PGVector in staging, evaluating compatibility with Pinecone and Milvus. Wants seamless routing: Redwood hosted API -> ingest -> vector DB, or serve directly from Redwood index if Dedicated supports it.
- Latency targets: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms for semantic search queries. Throughput/scale targets are main eval criteria.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget, looking for predictable unit economics; asks to compare hosted per-token/embed costs vs Dedicated reserved capacity pricing (committed monthly). Wants cost-per-1M-embeds model for decisioning.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML) required, SOC2 compliance required, audit logs + KMS integration mandatory. Data residency: US-only.
- Model preferences: prefer open models for embeddings (cost) but open to Redwood-verified models (better throughput/latency). Interested in quantized variants if quality meets thresholds.
- Routing/fallback: need automatic fallback to lower-capacity model variants during burst/backpressure; graceful degradation is a must for customer-facing search.

POC plan (agreed high-level):
- Phase 0 (hosted, 2 weeks): small-scale ingest (~500k rows) to validate end-to-end pipeline, measure latency & cost for embeddings + search.
- Phase 1 (hosted, 4 weeks): scale ingest to 5M rows, run nightly batch jobs, integrate with PGVector; measure throughput and index latency.
- Phase 2 (eval Dedicated): sizing exercise for reserved capacity (target baseline to hit 200k embeddings/hour and sustained search QPS); pricing proposal and SLA negotiation.

Notes from recent call:
- "We need hard numbers on cost if we hit 25M rows in production; our CFO won't sign until we see predictable unit economics." (Product lead)
